ConocoPhillips rose 0.89% today to $136.19, bouncing back after a sharp 3.9% drop on November 18th. The recovery comes as oil prices stabilized—U.S. crude is trading at $89.53 per barrel today, up from the lows that followed the Iran-Kuwait tensions and geopolitical uncertainty in the Strait of Hormuz earlier this week. The company benefits from higher global oil prices (at $92.94 per barrel) and signs that energy demand remains robust, particularly as the AI data center boom is expected to nearly double global electricity needs by 2030.

The permitting reform bill that passed the Senate this week also works in the energy sector's favor, potentially easing project development timelines. Combined with stabilizing crude prices and ongoing Middle East tensions that keep energy supplies uncertain, this provides some support for oil majors like ConocoPhillips.
